Subscribe to changes

Source: R/events.R
subscribe.Rd

Subscriptions call an R function when a document changes.

  • doc_subscribe() calls callback(event) for every committed change, whether made locally, imported from another replica, or caused by a checkout. With container, only changes to that container and the containers nested inside it are reported.

  • doc_subscribe_local_updates() calls callback(bytes) after each local commit with the update it produced: a raw vector that another replica can pass to doc_import(). This is the building block for live synchronization.

  • doc_subscribe_first_commit() calls callback(peer) the first time this document commits a local change under a given peer id, which is a natural moment to record who that peer is (for example in a map of authors). It fires again if the document's peer id changes, but not for peers whose changes are imported.

  • doc_subscribe_peer_id() calls callback(peer) with the new peer id whenever this document's own peer id changes.

  • unsubscribe() stops a subscription.

Usage

doc_subscribe(doc, callback, container = NULL)

doc_subscribe_local_updates(doc, callback)

doc_subscribe_first_commit(doc, callback)

doc_subscribe_peer_id(doc, callback)

unsubscribe(subscription)

Arguments

doc

A loro_doc.

callback

A function of one argument.

container

A container handle to limit the subscription to, or NULL for the whole document.

subscription

An object returned by one of the subscribe functions.

Value

The subscribe functions return a subscription object. unsubscribe() returns NULL invisibly.

Events

An event is a list with:

  • by: what caused the change: "local", "import", or "checkout".

  • origin: the origin label of the commit, usually "".

  • diff: the changes, in the format returned by doc_diff().

Timing

Changes are reported when they are committed, not when each edit is made, so call doc_commit() to flush pending edits. Callbacks run after the creditor function that committed or imported the change has finished its work, just before it returns, so a callback can safely read or edit the document. Events are delivered in the order they occurred: if a callback itself commits a change, the resulting event is delivered after the callbacks for the current event have run. An error in a callback is reported as a warning and does not interrupt the function that triggered it.

A subscription stays active until unsubscribe() is called, even if the object returned here is discarded and even after its document is no longer referenced, so unsubscribe when you are done. A document that is dropped with uncommitted edits commits them as it is freed, which can deliver one last event to a subscription left on it.

Examples

a = loro_doc()
b = loro_doc()

sync = doc_subscribe_local_updates(a, function(bytes) doc_import(b, bytes))
watch = doc_subscribe(b, function(event) {
  cat("b changed by", event$by, "\n")
})

text_insert(a, 1, "Hello")
doc_commit(a)
#> b changed by import 
text_get(b)
#> [1] "Hello"

unsubscribe(sync)
unsubscribe(watch)
